P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, but under CEMAC exchange control (Regulation 02/18/CEMAC/UMAC/CM). Service-export receipts must be collected and repatriated by the exporter through its domiciliary bank via the BEAC (art. 70). Service transactions of FCFA 5m or more must be domiciled with a CEMAC credit institution (art. 68) and backed by a contract, purchase order or invoice (art. 69). Foreign currency received by banks is surrendered to the BEAC.

sources.publisher: BEAC — Règlement n°02/18/CEMAC/UMAC/CM portant réglementation des changes
sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 70
sources.quote: Article 70. Les recettes d'exportation des services sont recouvrées et rapatriées par I'exportateur à travers sa banque domiciliataire par I'entremise de la Banque Centrale.

sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 68
sources.quote: Article 68. Les transactions avec I'extérieur liées aux services d'un montant égal ou supérieur à 5 millions de Francs CFA sont domiciliées auprès d'un établissement de crédit de la CEMAC.

P1_fx_receipts.notes: OCR text of the BEAC PDF (e.g. 'I'extérieur'); quotes copied as extracted. No specific repatriation deadline for services found (goods: 150 days). Later BEAC instructions not checked. Applies in all six CEMAC states.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: No. Opening a foreign-currency account within CEMAC for a resident is not authorised (art. 43). Only resident legal persons may be authorised by the BEAC. Resident individuals' accounts abroad must be declared to the BEAC (art. 42).

sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 43
sources.quote: Article 43. L'ouverture d'un compte en devises dans la CEMAC au profit d'un résident n'est pas autorisée.

sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 42
sources.quote: Article 42. Les comptes des personnes physiques résidentes ouverts à l'étranger sont déclarés à la Banque Centrale.

P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Central African Republic (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program. Restricted: Paddle lists it as an unsupported seller country; Lemon Squeezy blocks buyers there.

P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Wise: the CAR is NOT on Wise's list of countries whose residents can hold money. Payoneer: not confirmed. Under CEMAC rules, individuals must declare foreign accounts to the BEAC (P2).

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest: an individual enterprise (EI), with no legal minimum capital and unlimited liability. Formalities go through the GUFE (Guichet Unique de Formalités des Entreprises), created in 2008 in Bangui; a first regional branch opened in Bambari in September 2024. Current fees and timelines were not confirmed.

sources.quote: Il s'agit de la première antenne de ce type à être établie en préfecture, l’unique GUFE existant en République Centrafricaine (créé en 2008) jusqu’à lors, se trouvant à Bangui, la capitale du pays.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: A NIF (Numéro d'Identification Fiscale), obtained by registering with the tax administration (DGI); a 2026 guide lists it with the RCCM as required for a business.
L2_tax_id.note: Only one secondary domain (Africarrieres) captured; DGI procedure not found on 2026-10-22.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Reported regimes: a basic regime (SMT / Impôt Global Unique) for turnover under FCFA 30m, a simplified regime for FCFA 30–100m, and the real regime above FCFA 100m. Personal income tax on business income is reported at 30% (20% for agriculture). Treatment of foreign-source income was not established.
L3_income_tax_foreign.note: Single undated secondary source (Bakamba) for thresholds; CGI and current finance law not found on 2026-10-22; studies on IGU (12% of turnover) date from 2011–2016.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 19% on most goods and services; exports are zero-rated. Businesses with turnover of FCFA 30m or more collect VAT (reported by two secondary sources). Treatment of exported services was not established.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Law 24-001 on personal data protection applies, enforced by an independent administrative agency. Transfers abroad are allowed only to states with similar protection, unless an exception applies (consent, contract performance, etc.); transfers outside CEMAC/ECCAS need adequate protection. The law does not itself organise the agency, and whether the agency is operating was not confirmed.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: No e-commerce or electronic-transactions law was found. A Finance Ministry terms-of-reference document (undated, after Nov 2021) states the CAR has no law on electronic transactions and e-commerce. The 2018 electronic communications law (18.002) covers operators' privacy duties only. CEMAC consumer-protection directive 02/19 applies regionally.
L6_consumer_ecommerce.note: Absence rests on an undated (c. 2022) government ToR; no later e-commerce law found in searches on 2026-10-21/22, but currency not confirmed.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; PayPal is not available; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (2) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
